candidates.name: Custom browser UI + rosbridge_suite gateway
candidates.ros2_support: ROS 2 Humble rosbridge_suite WebSocket JSON API
candidates.streaming: WebSocket JSON subscriptions and client topic/service calls; compress/throttle large streams and measure serialization cost.
candidates.maps: Custom occupancy/terrain rendering, transforms, and time alignment are application work.
candidates.controls: Custom controls publish only to /lunabot/dashboard/command_request and read its status topic; implement explicit confirmations, with the ROS gateway enforcing freshness and allowed actions.
candidates.latency_resources: Not measured in this repository; JSON conversion and browser rendering need P9-03 measurement.
candidates.wsl_fit: WSL ROS gateway can serve Windows browser via localhost; DDS remains inside the ROS workspace.
candidates.license: rosbridge_suite BSD-3-Clause; web application dependency licenses must be tracked.
candidates.maintenance: Highest UI and telemetry implementation cost; maximum layout/control flexibility.

candidates.name: Foxglove Desktop/Web + Foxglove Bridge
candidates.ros2_support: Native ROS 2 bridge and Foxglove WebSocket data source; published ROS topic and service-call features are supported.
candidates.streaming: C++ bridge is documented as high performance/low overhead; bridge supports allowlists, message limits, QoS overrides, and connection options.
candidates.maps: Built-in 3D, Image, Plot, Raw Messages, and State Transitions panels cover most views; the 3D panel renders ROS OccupancyGrid. The separate Map panel is geospatial and is not the local SLAM map.
candidates.controls: Use a Foxglove/custom panel that publishes JSON only to /lunabot/dashboard/command_request and reads /lunabot/dashboard/control_status. The guarded gateway forwards allowed mission commands and invokes Trigger safety services; do not expose direct mission/service controls. Actions are not supported by the documented live connection feature matrix.
candidates.latency_resources: Not measured in this repository; C++ bridge is an implementation claim, not an observed rover benchmark.
candidates.wsl_fit: Run bridge in Ubuntu WSL and connect a Windows desktop/browser client to localhost; validate image/map load on this WSL host in P9-02/03.
candidates.license: ROS 2 bridge MIT; Foxglove visualization product uses plan/seat terms. Direct live connections require a Developer seat; verify current account plan before selecting it for release.
candidates.maintenance: Lowest initial panel work; mission-specific safe controls and timestamp/provenance checks need a custom extension or bounded wrapper.

candidates.name: Native Qt/Python + RViz2 + rqt plugins
candidates.ros2_support: Direct ROS 2 DDS using the existing Humble environment; RViz2 and rqt are maintained ROS packages.
candidates.streaming: Native ROS subscriptions avoid a browser gateway; local per-process queues/QoS still require explicit configuration.
candidates.maps: RViz2 already has project configurations and native OccupancyGrid, TF, image, point-cloud and marker displays.
candidates.controls: rqt service/topic plugins exist; a custom Qt panel should publish only to the guarded dashboard request topic and display gateway results.
candidates.latency_resources: Not measured for the six-view workload; existing WSL RViz use proves only that some GUI profiles work, not that the dashboard meets a budget.
candidates.wsl_fit: Best same-WSL process fit and WSLg can display Linux GUI apps; current repository reports RViz optional and some headless profiles are software-rendered.
candidates.license: RViz2 and rqt ROS packages are BSD-licensed; review all Qt/plugin dependencies when packaging.
candidates.maintenance: Medium-to-high custom UI work; direct ROS integration and no separate gateway.

selection_rationale: Prototype Foxglove Bridge plus its desktop client first: it has the broadest built-in coverage for synchronized images, 3D/map layers, plots, and service controls, reducing custom work for six views. This is a prototype choice, not a deployment approval. Compare the same topics and safety controls against native Qt in P9-02/03; if the required Developer seat is unavailable or the WSL resource/freshness gate fails, prefer the custom browser + BSD rosbridge path.
benchmark_policy: Do not infer UI latency/resource performance from bridge documentation or the P5 inference benchmark. Record render age from source stamp and local receive/render monotonic timestamps; include loaded camera/depth/map/point cloud and six views.
